Lessons.Title: Compare and Order Decimals and Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will compare and order fractions and decimals to the hundredths.
Key idea: Fractions and decimals with denominators 10 and 100 represent the same values and can be compared after making a common representation.
How to reason: Convert tenths and hundredths to equivalent place values before addition or comparing decimal distances.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up:  Number Talk: Sums of Fractions	 (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1:  Order Once, Order Twice	 (25 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\underline{\hspace{0.5in}} < \underline{\hspace{0.5in}}\), \(\underline{\hspace{0.5in}} > \underline{\hspace{0.5in}}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2:  Long Jumps	 (10 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as American athlete Carl Lewis won 10 Olympic medals and 10 World Championships in track and field—in 100-meter dash, 200-meter dash, and long jump., 1979, 8.13, 1980. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
Original source Cool-down is access-restricted/unverified; Edulytics substitutes goal-aligned independently authored teacher-reviewed exit prompt.
Edulytics worked model: Add five tenths and fifty hundredths.. Explain every transformation and check using equal wholes/units.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Mistaking 0.50 for 0.05 or equating a larger raw numerator to a greater fractional value.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It does not preserve the intended mathematical relationship or original task condition.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Convert tenths and hundredths to equivalent place values before addition or comparing decimal distances.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming that 0.5 and 0.05 are equal because both contain the digit five.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The 5 is in the tenths place in 0.5, and in the hundredths place in 0.05.
